text: Hi, I am Rani from Law World.
Today, I would be explaining you about Lok Adalats and how they serve as India's unique dispute resolution system.
Lok Adalat, meaning People's Court, is an alternative dispute resolution mechanism rooted in India's ancient tradition of community-based justice.
The first formal Lok Adalat was held in Gujarat on 14 March 1982.

They were later given statutory recognition under the Legal Services Authorities Act 1987, in line with sub-article A of Article 39 of the Constitution, which mandates free legal aid and equal justice for all.
Under Section 19 of the Act, Legal Services Authorities at the Supreme Court, State, District and Taluk levels can organise Lok Adalats.
They handle both pending court cases and pre-litigation disputes with the consent of both parties.
Under Section 21, every award passed by a Lok Adalat is deemed a decree of a civil court.
It is final, binding and no appeal lies against it.
Lok Adalats have no court fees, follow no strict procedural rules and cannot deal with non-compoundable criminal offences.
They have been instrumental in reducing the massive backlog of cases in Indian courts.
Thanks for watching this quick breakdown of Lok Adalats.
